                <Attribute Type="public definition">Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is typically defined by the presence of unexplained left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH). Such LVH occurs in a non-dilated ventricle in the absence of other cardiac or systemic disease capable of producing the observed magnitude of increased LV wall thickness, such as pressure overload (e.g., long-standing hypertension, aortic stenosis) or storage/infiltrative disorders (e.g., Fabry disease, amyloidosis). The clinical manifestations of HCM range from asymptomatic LVH to progressive heart failure to sudden cardiac death (SCD), and vary from individual to individual even within the same family. Common symptoms include shortness of breath (particularly with exertion), chest pain, palpitations, orthostasis, presyncope, and syncope. Most often the LVH of HCM becomes apparent during adolescence or young adulthood, although it may also develop late in life, in infancy, or in childhood.</Attribute>

              <Attribute Type="Description">Among 7 individuals with sporadic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (CMH1; 192600), Watkins et al. (1992) identified mutations in the beta cardiac MHC genes in 2. Since the parents were neither clinically nor genetically affected, the authors concluded that the mutations in each proband arose de novo. In summary, this variant meets criteria to be classified as pathogenic for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in an autosomal dominant manner. The benign evidence code BP2 was not considered to be in conflict with this conclusion given that presence of a second variant can be seen in individuals with cardiomyopathy and may contribute to the severity of disease. For these reasons, this variant has been classified as Pathogenic.</Comment>
